Import a scenario

Choose a radar-network-scenario.json file (it imports at once) or paste its text. The page checks the schema, units, domain and finite values; the current scene stays if the check fails.

VisualsRadarWorks offline

Radar network: the range equation in 3D

Three moving radars and four moving targets give 36 links, one for each transmitter, receiver and target. Each link shows its radar equation, numbers, SNR, detector threshold, required SNR and margin. Move the objects or the time and see which factor changes the result.

All absolute values are synthetic: power, gains, losses, RCS and the clutter patches. Only the carriers (4, 10 and 17 GHz) come from the supplied evidence. The NASA F-117 model curves stay in a separate evidence panel. Their magnitude reference is not stated, so they never enter a power or range result.

3D scene

The 3D renderer is not available in this browser. The link table, the numeric controls and every calculation still work.

radar target monostatic path bistatic path clutter patch

ρ1 is the single-pulse matched-filter SNR. Margin is ρ1 minus the required single-pulse SNR for the detector settings. An inactive or invalid link keeps its row and its reason; its result is never replaced by zero. Static table: initial scene at t = 0 s, model digest a0070256242b0dce3e93220e967bd353.

Controls

Every value in the scene has a numeric control here. Edits pause time, enter the undo history with their time, and recalculate the analytic results at once. Sampled results then show “Result from previous parameters” until you recalculate.

Model, sources and limits

What the model does

Each link (transmitter, receiver, target) uses the bistatic radar equation with linear units inside products, the single-pulse matched-filter SNR ρ₁ = Prτ/(kTsLMF), and a thermal-noise square-law detector after ideal coherent (or noncoherent) integration. Positions come from state and time: p(t) = p₀ + vt or piecewise-linear waypoints. Right-handed frame: x east, y north, z up; SI units inside. Positive Doppler means approach.

Sampled processing uses synthetic complex baseband: a band-limited fractional-delay filter, per-sample carrier phase from the linear path-length model, a unit-energy matched filter and a windowed slow-time DFT. Analytic thermal-noise probabilities do not establish Pfa or Pd in clutter or interference; the page shows sampled estimates separately.
